solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Publicity video new duke supplied (8)

indicatorNotes.new: a new version of a word is a remade one, so VIDEO's letters are made over in a fresh order

annotation.surface: A promotional film has been handed over by a newly created duke.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'new duke' as one idea, but 'new' belongs to 'video' and the duke stands alone as D.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods that were supplied were furnished, handed over, given.

entries.clue: What may enlarge as it gets dimmer students (6)

annotation.definition: What may enlarge as it gets dimmer
annotation.definitionNote: The first definition describes one pupil; the answer is plural to match 'students'.

blocks.clueFragment: What may enlarge as it gets dimmer
blocks.note: the dark opening in the eye widens in low light

annotation.surface: A riddle about something that grows as the light fades, trailing off into students.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a riddle for the eye's pupil, which widens in the dark; the second is the plain school sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the eye's opening dilates in dim light, and school students are its namesakes.

entries.clue: Old cat, losing it, turned man-eater (6)

indicatorNotes.losing: something lost is no longer there, so the letters IT drop out of the cat

annotation.surface: An ageing cat lost its temper and became a man-eater.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing it' looks like the cat flying into a rage; here it tells you to remove the letters I and T from TIGRESS.
annotation.definitionFit: In folklore an ogre's diet is people, and the female of the kind is a man-eater in the literal sense.

entries.clue: Device put into effect (9)

blocks.note: carry out a plan or policy

annotation.surface: A gadget has been brought into operation.
annotation.walkthrough: The noun and the verb are spelt the same; the clue reads as one phrase but splits after 'Device'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one spelling: the noun is a tool such as a garden device, the verb means carry out.

entries.clue: Retract weapons after English make amends (3,4,5)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' places the weapons later in the answer than the English and the amends

blocks.note: to atone is to make amends

annotation.surface: Put down your arms, since the English must make up for past wrongs.
annotation.walkthrough: The breaks fall differently from the answer's: E + ATONE + SWORDS regroups as EAT ONE'S WORDS.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to take back something said, humbly admitting it was wrong.

entries.clue: Drink for everyone abandoning a conspirator (6)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: to abandon is to walk out and leave, so U departs from the conspirator's name

blocks.note: Cassius, one of Julius Caesar's assassins
U = universal, the film rating for all ages; removed

annotation.surface: A round of drinks for all, leaving out one plotter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For everyone' is not generosity but the U film certificate, suitable for all audiences, taken out of CASSIUS.
annotation.definitionFit: A drink by example: a blackcurrant liqueur from France, the base of a kir.

entries.clue: Meeting place ready for Israel’s smallest unit (5)

blocks.note: the public square of an ancient Greek city
'ready' = cash; the coin worth a hundredth of a shekel

annotation.surface: A venue set up for Israel's tiniest military unit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for money (as in 'the readies'), so the second half asks for Israel's smallest coin, the agora.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the assembly square of a Greek city, and the Hebrew-named hundredth part of the Israeli shekel.

entries.clue: Language Society cryptic ranks above sex (8)

indicatorNotes.cryptic: something cryptic is obscured, so RANKS appears with its letters disguised
indicatorNotes.above: in a down entry what is above comes first, so the ranks sit on top of the sex

blocks.note: 'it' = sex appeal or sex, as in 'It girl'

annotation.surface: A linguistics society's puzzling hierarchy puts rank before sex.
annotation.walkthrough: IT for sex is an old convention from 'It', meaning sex appeal.
annotation.definitionFit: A language by example: the classical tongue of ancient India and of Hindu scripture.

entries.clue: Sharp decline in poverty (8)

blocks.note: abrupt, curt, as in a sharp reply

annotation.surface: A steep fall in living standards pushing people into poverty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharp decline' reads as one economic phrase, but each word is a separate piece and 'poverty' is the definition, in its sense of scarcity.
annotation.definitionFit: Poverty can mean a scarcity or lack, as in 'a poverty of ideas'.

entries.clue: Paddy infiltrating soldiers’ defences (8)

indicatorNotes.infiltrating: an infiltrator slips inside enemy lines, so the fit of temper slips inside the soldiers

blocks.note: a paddy and a pet are both fits of temper

annotation.surface: An Irishman sneaking through the troops' fortifications.
annotation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name; it is British slang for a tantrum, and so is 'pet', as in 'in a pet'.
annotation.definitionFit: The low protective walls along a rampart or trench shield those behind them, so they are defences.

entries.clue: Put up with Love Island (6)

annotation.surface: Tolerating the reality TV show Love Island.
annotation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show, so the words hang together; the split falls between 'Love' and 'Island'.
annotation.definitionFit: An island by example: the huge South-East Asian island shared by Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

entries.clue: Outfit wife dons to work on case (3-5,4)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on clothing, so TO wraps itself around W
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry one piece sits on another by coming after it, so the case goes last

blocks.note: used as it stands, wrapped around W
a work, as in a piece of music

annotation.surface: The wife puts on an outfit to go and work on a legal case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' has the wife dressing; in the wordplay it is TO that wears W. 'Case' is a lawsuit, not luggage.
annotation.definitionFit: A matching jacket with trousers or skirt makes a complete outfit.

entries.clue: Fine cotton reel’s last inch (5)

indicatorNotes.last: the last of reel is its final letter, L

blocks.note: an inch is a small Scottish island, as in Inchcolm

annotation.surface: The final inch of thread on a reel of fine cotton.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a length of thread; in Scotland an inch is a small island, so it gives ISLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a smooth, tightly twisted cotton thread once used for stockings.

entries.clue: Racecourse punters not exploited yet (9)

annotation.surface: At the races, the bettors are fresh and nobody has fleeced them yet.
annotation.walkthrough: Punters look like racecourse gamblers but are customers here, and an untapped customer base is a new market.
annotation.definitionFit: A racecourse by example: the Suffolk town in England that is the historic home of British horse racing.

entries.clue: Go without a small, sweet dish (5,7)

indicatorNotes.without: in its old sense 'without' means outside, so PEE stands outside A and S

blocks.note: in Britain the sweet course is called this

annotation.surface: Skip the little dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go without' reads as 'do without'; here 'without' means outside. Pease pudding is savoury, so 'sweet dish' is not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A dish by example: boiled split peas mashed with ham, a traditional food of north-east England.

entries.clue: Front of tatty, dog-eared novel made to look inferior (9)

indicatorNotes.Front of: the front of a word is its first letter, T
indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new and original, so the letters take a new form

annotation.surface: A scruffy, well-thumbed paperback novel looks shabby from its cover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as the tatty book itself; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: To derogate is to disparage or belittle, so the past participle means made to look inferior.

entries.clue: Clobber worn by sub playing okay (6-2)

indicatorNotes.worn by: clothing worn by someone goes round them, so THUMP wraps the sub
indicatorNotes.playing: something playing is in lively motion, so SUB's letters move

blocks.note: to clobber is to hit hard

annotation.surface: A substitute footballer on the pitch, wearing his kit.
annotation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes, which suits 'worn by'; here it is the verb meaning to hit.
annotation.definitionFit: A raised-thumb sign is a gesture of approval, a nod that says okay.

entries.clue: Head runs out of school preserve (8)

indicatorNotes.out of: what runs out of a place leaves it, so R leaves TRAIN

annotation.surface: The headteacher dashes out of school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' and 'school' paint a headteacher; 'school' is the verb meaning train.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to keep something in good condition, as one preserves an old building.

entries.clue: Red card leads to another frank exchange (5-2-5)

blocks.note: a card from one of the two red suits
a second red card of the same kind

annotation.surface: A footballer's sending-off sparks a blunt argument.
annotation.walkthrough: The red card looks like a football sending-off; it is a playing card from the hearts suit, led to another of the same suit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a candid, intimate talk in which both people speak openly.

entries.clue: Hi-fi using disc before case of tapes turned up (6)

indicatorNotes.case of: a case is the outside of something, so take the outer letters of tapes
indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down entry, turning something up means it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a disc is round, like O

annotation.surface: A sound system playing a record, with the cassette box flipped over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disc' and 'tapes' belong to the hi-fi picture, but the disc is only a circle, O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a two-channel sound system is what people mean by a hi-fi.

entries.clue: Final exam over, covered in mistakes (6)

indicatorNotes.covered in: something covered in a coating is surrounded by it, so O is surrounded by TRIPS

annotation.surface: The finals have ended, and the paper was full of errors.
annotation.walkthrough: The mistakes look like the candidate's errors on the paper; they are TRIPS, as in trips of the tongue.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Cambridge University's name for its final honours degree examination.

entries.clue: Tug crew take care of (9)

blocks.note: to crew a ship is to staff it

annotation.surface: A tugboat's crew look after their vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tug crew' reads as a tugboat's sailors; 'Tug' is the verb and 'crew' the verb too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to haul or shove roughly by hand is to tug.

entries.clue: Beer crate regularly dropped on your toes (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly dropped: letters dropped at regular intervals means every other one goes, keeping R and T of crate

blocks.note: C, A and E go, leaving R and T

annotation.surface: A crate of beer keeps falling on your feet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface drops the crate on real toes; 'on your toes' is the idiom for watchful.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone on their toes is poised and ready, which is watchful and quick to react.

entries.clue: Snapper’s part in shaming a Tory (5)

indicatorNotes.part in: a part of something lies inside it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

annotation.surface: A photographer's role in humiliating a Conservative politician.
annotation.walkthrough: A snapper looks like a press photographer; it is anything that snaps, here an alligator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the short form of alligator, a reptile known for its snapping jaws.

entries.clue: Wound exposed on front of shark (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, one piece put on another is added after it
indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter, S

annotation.surface: An open injury on the shark's snout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury; it is the past tense of wind, as a road winds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym of the verb: a river that wound through the valley twisted and turned like a serpent.

entries.clue: Flatter bloomer, less cooked on top (6,2)

indicatorNotes.less: less means minus, so the letter that follows is subtracted
indicatorNotes.on top: in an across clue the top of a word is its first letter, C of cooked

blocks.note: a bloomer is a flower; this one is yellow

annotation.surface: A loaf of bread, underbaked, with a flatter top.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer is also a British loaf, which is why 'cooked' fits the surface; here it is a flowering plant.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to lay on praise so as to win a favour, smoothing someone as butter smooths bread.

entries.clue: Party animal twisting to the hits (6)

annotation.definition: Party animal twisting to the hits

blocks.note: the surface wants a keen reveller; read literally it is an animal-shaped object at a children's party
the surface has dancing to chart songs; really it is spinning on its string as it is struck

annotation.surface: A reveller dancing the twist to chart hits.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a keen partygoer dancing to pop hits; read literally, it is a papier-mâché animal at a party, spinning as it is struck until the sweets fall out.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a papier-mâché figure, often an animal, hung up and hit at parties.

entries.clue: Careful bosses keeping note of liabilities (8)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so STUDS hold IOU inside

blocks.note: a written note of a debt: 'I owe you'
a boss is a raised knob on a surface

annotation.surface: Prudent managers keep a record of what the firm owes.
annotation.walkthrough: Bosses look like managers; they are ornamental studs.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: studious can mean deliberate and painstaking, as in studious attention to detail.
